The housing element is an eight-year plan that assesses the condition of housing in the city, establishes a roadmap for accommodating the projected housing demand, and sets citywide goals, objectives, and policies for housing and the housing needs of the community. We are currently in the sixth cycle of the housing element, which plans for the period of 2023 to 2031. The Six Cycle Housing Element was adopted by the City Council on January 10, 2023, and certified by HCDE, the State Department of Housing and Community Development, on March 22, 2023. The Annual Progress Report, or APR, is required to be submitted to the State every year by April 1 to report on the City's progress on housing production for the prior calendar year and the City's efforts to implement the housing element programs that are aimed to protect the housing stability of existing residents, preserve and improve the existing housing stock, and produce new housing at all income levels. The state assigns a RHNA number to each council of governments. The council of governments for the Bay Area is known as ABAG, the Association of Bay Area Governments. ABAG was assigned 441,176 units for the six-cycle housing element. ABAC then distributes those units to each Bay Area city and county. Fremont was assigned 12,897 units that it needs to plan for within the 2023 to 2031 planning period, broken down into four income categories.
